column8: One month after birth, listing feeding and pumping lessons nobody told her plainly.
column9: A lot of advice you get is “take good care of your nipples” but not really what that entails.

column8: She bought a wearable pump as her only pump and regretted it.
column9: I had gotten a wearable pump as my primary and only pump. Girl don’t do it. First off the wearables have 10000 parts that need to be cleaned.

column8: Wishes she had known pumping basics sooner; she had been stockpiling milk for daycare.
column9: See and if I had know this I wouldn’t have stressed myself out so bad trying to feed the freezer for day care.

column8: Replying about her first month of searching for answers.
column9: My Google is TIRED after this month I have looked up so many ridiculous things. Analysis paralysis is so real.

column8: Overdue personal trainer, near bed-bound most of pregnancy, says she no longer recognises herself.
column9: Which then meant I haven’t been able to work much, or keep active which is hugely important to me as I’m a personal trainer. I feel like I don’t feel like myself at all anymore, and now I’m overdue.

column8: Her midwife and doctors call her pain normal; she agrees but feels lost.
column9: My midwife and Drs say it’s normal and of course it is, but I don’t recognise myself at the moment.

column8: Third pregnancy at 15 weeks, hoping to breastfeed this time; sore nipples unlike before.
column9: I don’t remember having such painful sensitive nipples during pregnancy. This is awful. Changing clothes is awful. Showering is awful. Sleeping is awful. They hurt SO bad.

column8: After two earlier babies she could not breastfeed, she hoped this time would differ.
column9: I’ve been so excited at the idea of hopefully getting to successfully breastfeed this time…. But now I’m worried.

column8: At 32 weeks with swelling, working at a desk from home, unsure she can work until birth.
column9: I didn’t plan on taking my leave until it was time to give birth but I don’t know if I’m gonna make it that far.

column8: Smooth pregnancy until the third trimester started.
column9: So I spoke to soon about how smooth everything was with my pregnancy and the almost right after entering this trimester everything for bad .

column8: Venting at strangers online who second-guess doctors' c-section advice; lists lines she has seen.
column9: Statements like: “Your pelvis is definitely not too small.” “Everyone can give birth vaginally.” “Don’t let them pressure you into a c-section.” “Your body was made for this.”

column8: Venting about online pressure over birth choices; possibly AI-polished post.
column9: Birth is not an ideology. It is medicine. And every woman’s situation is different.

column8: Husband's demanding job always comes first; she fears the same after the baby.
column9: I am just worried that when I actually have this baby everything is still going to go to the job first and I'm going to be stuck at home with a baby.

column8: Since the first trimester ended, her husband pushes errands back to her.
column9: Now that I'm out of first tri it's been a lot more "Why can't YOU do that"

column8: First-time mother imagining her husband refusing to leave work early when she needs him.
column9: I'm imagining a situation where there's something going on with the baby that I feel I can't do myself, I ask him to come home early and finish the day at home to help me, and he refuses because he "has a meeting".

column8: At 32 weeks, told to follow up quickly, she cannot get her OB office to call back.
column9: The way my OB office works is you talk to a triage person, not anyone in the actual office.

column8: Days of calls after a hospital visit with no callback from her OB office.
column9: It has been 6 days since I went to L&D and 5 days since my first call and my office will not call me back.

column8: Late-pregnancy prescription mix-ups between midwives and the pharmacy.
column9: every midwife I spoke to seemed to not know any details & just fob me off with ‘I’ll put another prescription in for you’ which obv never materialised

column8: Asking strangers whether her annoyance at admin delays in her care is fair.
column9: Am I justified in feeling annoyed about how this was handled/admin delays etc or am I being a Karen?

column8: Eight months pregnant; guests ignored her carefully researched registry.
column9: Yet almost all the gifts I got were cute, impractical clothes and more than 50 pairs of newborn socks (not kidding).

column8: How she built the registry nobody followed.
column9: I spent so much time and effort researching and combing through all the necessary items we needed. I tried to keep everything in the low-to-mid price range while reading thousands of reviews on products across the internet.

column8: Her mother bought a bassinet and carrier already marked purchased on the registry.
column9: My mom replied, “Oh, well it won’t hurt to have extras.”

column8: Guests' answer to duplicate gifts at her shower.
column9: The guests’ reactions were awkward, but their response was, “Oh, you can just go to the stores and return/exchange them.”

column8: Replying to a commenter's large registry; she sees registries as a checklist plus a discount.
column9: $5100 is insane. Don't get me wrong. I can see why some people view baby registries as a way to exploit others for overpriced gear that parents simply don't want to spend their own money on.

column8: Why she still values a registry.
column9: registries offer parents a 10% to 20% completion discount close to the due date.

column8: At 8 weeks with no appetite, eating junk food, she blames herself.
column9: I’ve barely had an appetite, I’m struggling to eat proper meals, and I’ve mostly been surviving on chips, fast food, and random snacks.

column8: Explains why she ordered takeout through early pregnancy.
column9: I just couldn't stand the idea of cooking anything and the only thing that sounded good to me was ordering take out

column8: At 7 weeks, researching everything from cribs to schooling and unable to focus on anything else.
column9: I'm only 7 weeks pregnant and I feel like I am overwhelming myself with loads of research.

column8: What her research list has grown to at 7 weeks; she already built an unshared registry.
column9: Now, I'm looking into public schools, private schools, nature & forest schools, and homeschooling options. I am very so overwhelmed but also so impatient I just want to have my LO already.

column8: The line that pregnancy is enjoyable, set against how she feels at 7 weeks.
column9: Everyone says that they enjoy being pregnant but idk how I'm going to handle feeling like this for 8 more months also with feeling like crap from pregnancy.

column8: At 24 weeks with near-daily head pain since early pregnancy, nothing has helped.
column9: I am feeling totally defeated by the dead ends I’m reaching when it comes to finding answers and/or relief.
